circuit:Abu Dhabi.title: Yas Marina Circuit
circuit:Abu Dhabi.summary: Yas Marina Circuit is a 5. 281-kilometre track located on Yas Island in Abu Dhabi that was designed by Hermann Tilke and has served as the venue for Formula One's season finale since 2009. The circuit represents the second of four Middle Eastern Formula One venues, following Bahrain's establishment and preceding the later additions of Qatar and Saudi Arabia.

circuit:Australia.title: Albert Park Circuit
circuit:Australia.summary: The Albert Park Circuit is a street course encircling Albert Park Lake in Melbourne that hosts the Australian Grand Prix as its primary Formula One event, along with various support categories including the Supercars Championship round. The venue maintains an FIA Grade 1 classification for motorsport racing.

circuit:Austria.title: Red Bull Ring
circuit:Austria.summary: Located in Spielberg, Austria, this 4. 326 km circuit began hosting the Austrian Grand Prix in 1970 and maintained that role for 18 years before a lengthy absence. Following significant reconstruction and shortening work, the track resumed its position on the Formula One calendar from 1997 onwards, accommodating the Austrian Grand Prix once more.

circuit:Azerbaijan.title: Baku City Circuit
circuit:Azerbaijan.summary: The Baku City Circuit is a street track in Azerbaijan's capital, spanning 6. 003 km to rank as Formula One's fourth-longest venue. The circuit first hosted the European Grand Prix in 2016 before transitioning to the Azerbaijan Grand Prix from 2017 onwards, both organized by the Baku City Circuit Operation Company.

circuit:Bahrain.title: Bahrain International Circuit
circuit:Bahrain.summary: Opened in 2004, the Bahrain International Circuit spans 5. 412 km and hosted the first Formula One grand prix in the Middle East that same year. The FIA Grade 1-licensed venue accommodates various racing categories including drag racing, GP2 Series, endurance competitions, and the annual Formula One race, with multiple configuration options available on the track.

circuit:Barcelona.title: Circuit de Barcelona-Catalunya
circuit:Barcelona.summary: Located in Montmeló near Barcelona, this 4. 657-kilometer Spanish racing circuit is renowned as a versatile venue featuring a balanced mix of high-speed straights and diverse corner configurations that test multiple aspects of driver and car performance. The track holds an FIA Grade 1 certification and can accommodate approximately 140,700 spectators across its grandstands.

circuit:Belgium.title: Circuit de Spa-Francorchamps
circuit:Belgium.summary: Situated in the Walloon region of Belgium near the town of Spa, this 7. 004 km circuit hosts the Belgian Grand Prix and has been a fixture of Formula One since the inaugural 1950 season. The track has maintained continuous Grand Prix racing from 1985 onward, with only two exceptions in 2003 and 2006.

circuit:Canada.title: Circuit Gilles Villeneuve
circuit:Canada.summary: Located on Montreal's Notre Dame Island, this 4. 361-kilometer Canadian circuit serves as the permanent home of the Formula One Canadian Grand Prix. Beyond its F1 events, the track has accommodated various international racing series including sportscar championships and North American racing competitions.

circuit:China.title: Shanghai International Circuit
circuit:China.summary: Located in Shanghai's Jiading District, this Chinese motorsport facility gained prominence as the host of the Chinese Grand Prix, which ran annually from 2004 to 2019 before returning in 2024. The venue has expanded its racing calendar to include electric vehicle racing events beginning in 2024.

circuit:Great Britain.title: Silverstone Circuit
circuit:Great Britain.summary: Located near Silverstone in Northamptonshire, England, this circuit hosted the inaugural World Championship race in 1950 and has been the permanent home of the British Grand Prix since 1987, after sharing hosting duties with two other venues for over three decades. The track also serves as the venue for the British round of motorcycle racing's premier series.

circuit:Hungary.title: Hungaroring
circuit:Hungary.summary: The Hungaroring, located near Budapest in Mogyoród, hosted Formula One's first Grand Prix held within the Eastern Bloc when it opened in 1986, following Bernie Ecclestone's interest in bringing the sport behind the Iron Curtain. Built remarkably quickly over just eight months starting in late 1985, the 4. 381 km circuit was constructed outside the city near a major highway rather than as a street course in Budapest's central park as initially envisioned.

circuit:Italy.title: Autodromo Nazionale Monza
circuit:Italy.summary: The Autodromo Nazionale Monza is a 5. 793 km Italian racing circuit constructed in 1922 near Milan, making it Europe's oldest purpose-built track and only the third of its kind globally. Home to the Italian Grand Prix since 1949 (excepting 1980 during renovation), the venue earns its nickname "Temple of Speed" from its notably long straights and fast-paced corners.

circuit:Japan.title: Suzuka International Racing Course
circuit:Japan.summary: Located in Mie Prefecture, Japan, the Suzuka Circuit is a 5. 807 km figure-eight track operated by Honda Mobilityland that regularly hosts Formula One racing and other premier motorsport events. With a spectator capacity of 155,000, it ranks among the world's most prestigious venues for international racing championships.

circuit:Las Vegas.title: Las Vegas Strip Circuit
circuit:Las Vegas.summary: The Las Vegas Strip Circuit is a street course that navigates through Paradise, Nevada, weaving along portions of the famous Las Vegas Boulevard where the city's premier hospitality venues and gaming establishments are concentrated. The layout passes iconic destinations such as the MSG Sphere, Caesars Palace, Bellagio, and Paris Las Vegas, integrating these recognizable structures into the racing route.

circuit:Mexico City.title: Autódromo Hermanos Rodríguez
circuit:Mexico City.summary: Located in Mexico City, the 4. 304 km Autódromo Hermanos Rodríguez honours two racing brothers who died in separate accidents. The circuit has hosted Formula One's Mexican Grand Prix in multiple eras, resuming the race in 2015 after a 23-year absence and currently running it under the Mexico City Grand Prix designation.

circuit:Miami.title: Miami International Autodrome
circuit:Miami.summary: The Miami International Autodrome is a temporary street circuit constructed around Hard Rock Stadium in Miami Gardens, featuring 3. 363 miles of track with 19 turns and an average qualifying speed near 139 mph. Designed specifically by racing circuit specialists for Formula One competition, the venue was established as a new calendar addition beginning with the 2022 championship season.

circuit:Monaco.title: Circuit de Monaco
circuit:Monaco.summary: The Circuit de Monaco is a street-based racing venue spanning 3. 337 kilometers through the streets of Monte Carlo and La Condamine, circling the harbor of the principality. The track is widely known by the name "Monte Carlo" due to its predominant location within that particular district of Monaco.

circuit:Netherlands.title: Circuit Zandvoort
circuit:Netherlands.summary: Located in the Dutch coastal dunes west of Amsterdam, Circuit Zandvoort is a 4. 259 km track that hosted the revived Dutch Grand Prix starting in 2021, though this Formula One arrangement concludes after 2026. The venue, situated near the North Sea, has carried various official names throughout its history, most recently adopting a sponsorship designation.

circuit:Qatar.title: Lusail International Circuit
circuit:Qatar.summary: The Lusail International Circuit is a Qatari motor racing venue situated north of Doha near the city of Lusail. Spanning 5. 419 kilometers with a 1.

circuit:São Paulo.title: Autódromo José Carlos Pace
circuit:São Paulo.summary: Interlagos is a 4. 309 km counterclockwise racing venue situated in São Paulo, Brazil, which opened in 1940 and was later renamed in 1985 to commemorate Formula One driver José Carlos Pace following his fatal aviation accident. The circuit features a karting facility dedicated to another Brazilian racing legend and now serves as the final resting place of the driver it is named after.

circuit:Saudi Arabia.title: Jeddah Corniche Circuit
circuit:Saudi Arabia.summary: The Jeddah Corniche Circuit is a street racing venue located along Saudi Arabia's Red Sea coastline, hosting the Saudi Arabian Grand Prix since 2021. The track has also welcomed international electric racing events beginning in 2025.

circuit:Singapore.title: Marina Bay Street Circuit
circuit:Singapore.summary: The Marina Bay Street Circuit winds through Singapore's downtown waterfront, incorporating the Downtown Core and Kallang districts within its layout.

circuit:Spain.title: Circuit de Barcelona-Catalunya
circuit:Spain.summary: Located in Montmeló near Barcelona, this Spanish circuit spans 4. 657 kilometres and features a balanced mix of high-speed straights and diverse corner configurations that challenge drivers across multiple disciplines. The venue holds FIA Grade 1 certification and accommodates over 140,000 spectators across its grandstands.

circuit:United States.title: Circuit of the Americas
circuit:United States.summary: The Circuit of the Americas in Austin, Texas spans 3. 426 miles and operates to the highest FIA standards, hosting multiple racing series including Formula One's United States Grand Prix, MotoGP, and World Endurance Championship events. Beyond these marquee competitions, the venue has accommodated various other motorsport categories ranging from IndyCar to rallycross and sports car championships throughout its operational history.

driver:ALB.title: Alexander Albon
driver:ALB.summary: Alexander Albon, a Thai and British motorsport competitor, represents Thailand on the Formula One grid with Williams.

driver:ALO.title: Fernando Alonso
driver:ALO.summary: The Spanish driver currently races for Aston Martin in Formula One, having secured two world championship titles during his tenure at Renault in 2005 and 2006. Across his 23-season career, Alonso has claimed 32 Grand Prix victories and achieved considerable success in endurance racing, including two Le Mans 24 Hours wins with Toyota and the 2018-19 World Endurance Championship, making him the sole driver to win both top-level Formula One and World Endurance championships.

driver:ANT.title: Andrea Kimi Antonelli
driver:ANT.summary: Italian driver Andrea Kimi Antonelli represents Mercedes in Formula One, having secured six Grand Prix victories since entering the championship in 2025.

driver:BEA.title: Oliver Bearman
driver:BEA.summary: Oliver Bearman is a British motorsport competitor who currently drives for the Haas Formula One team.

driver:BOR.title: Gabriel Bortoleto
driver:BOR.summary: Brazilian driver Gabi Bortoleto currently races in Formula One for Audi, bringing his competitive spirit to one of the sport's established manufacturers.

driver:BOT.title: Valtteri Bottas
driver:BOT.summary: Valtteri Bottas, a Finnish driver, currently races for Cadillac in Formula One following a lengthy career that included two runner-up finishes in the drivers' championship while competing for Mercedes in 2019 and 2020. Over his 13 seasons in the sport, he has secured 10 Grand Prix victories.

driver:COL.title: Franco Colapinto
driver:COL.summary: Franco Alejandro Colapinto is an Argentine racing driver currently competing in Formula One for the Alpine team.

driver:DOO.title: Jack Doohan (racing driver)
driver:DOO.summary: Jack Doohan, an Australian motorsport competitor, holds a reserve driving position with Haas while pursuing his primary racing commitments in European endurance competition. The 2024-2025 season saw him participate in seven Formula One races across these roles.

driver:GAS.title: Pierre Gasly
driver:GAS.summary: French driver Pierre Gasly currently races for Alpine in Formula One. He previously achieved his sole Grand Prix victory at the 2020 Italian Grand Prix while competing for AlphaTauri.

driver:HAD.title: Isack Hadjar
driver:HAD.summary: Hadjar is a French-Algerian driver who represents France in Formula One, currently driving for Red Bull Racing.

driver:HAM.title: Lewis Hamilton
driver:HAM.summary: Lewis Hamilton is a British Formula One driver currently racing for Ferrari who shares the record for most championship titles with seven victories, equalling Michael Schumacher's achievement. He also holds multiple individual records including the greatest number of race wins, pole positions, and podium appearances in the sport's history.

driver:HUL.title: Nico Hülkenberg
driver:HUL.summary: German driver Nicolas Hülkenberg currently races in Formula One for Audi. Beyond his single-seater career, he achieved a major milestone by winning the prestigious 24 Hours of Le Mans in 2015 as part of the Porsche team.

driver:LAW.title: Liam Lawson
driver:LAW.summary: Liam Lawson, a New Zealand motorsport competitor, currently drives for Racing Bulls in the Formula One championship series.

driver:LEC.title: Charles Leclerc
driver:LEC.summary: Charles Leclerc, a driver from Monaco, represents Ferrari in Formula One competition. He achieved second place in the 2022 drivers' championship while with the Scuderia and has secured nine race victories throughout his nine seasons in the sport.

driver:MAG.title: Kevin Magnussen
driver:MAG.summary: Danish racing driver Kevin Magnussen currently competes in endurance racing for BMW through the WRT team while also pursuing a part-time NASCAR career with Trackhouse Racing. His previous Formula One tenure spanned two separate periods between 2014 and 2024, with a break in between.

driver:NOR.title: Lando Norris
driver:NOR.summary: Lando Norris, a British driver for McLaren, claimed the 2025 Formula One World Drivers' Championship after competing in the sport for eight seasons. He has secured 12 Grand Prix victories throughout his career in the championship.

driver:OCO.title: Esteban Ocon
driver:OCO.summary: Esteban Ocon, a French racing driver, currently competes in Formula One for Haas. He previously achieved a Grand Prix victory at the 2021 Hungarian Grand Prix while driving for Alpine.

driver:PER.title: Sergio Pérez
driver:PER.summary: Sergio "Checo" Pérez represents Mexico in Formula One racing for Cadillac. The veteran driver finished second in the 2023 championship standings while with Red Bull and has accumulated six Grand Prix victories over his 15-year career in the sport.

driver:PIA.title: Oscar Piastri
driver:PIA.summary: Oscar Piastri, an Australian driver, currently races for McLaren in Formula One, where he has secured nine Grand Prix victories throughout his four seasons in the sport.

driver:RIC.title: Daniel Ricciardo
driver:RIC.summary: Daniel Ricciardo, an Australian driver known by the nickname "the Honey Badger," competed in Formula One for 14 seasons between 2011 and 2024, securing eight Grand Prix victories during his career before retiring from the sport.

driver:RUS.title: George Russell (racing driver)
driver:RUS.summary: British driver George Russell currently races for Mercedes in Formula One, where he has accumulated seven Grand Prix victories throughout his eight-season tenure in the sport.

driver:SAI.title: Carlos Sainz Jr.
driver:SAI.summary: Spanish driver Carlos Sainz competes for Williams in Formula One, where he has claimed four Grand Prix victories over his 12-season career in the sport.

driver:SAR.title: Logan Sargeant
driver:SAR.summary: Logan Sargeant is an American driver who currently races in the FIA World Endurance Championship's LMGT3 category with Proton Competition, having previously competed in IMSA's LMP2 class. His Formula One career spanned 2023 to 2024.

driver:STR.title: Lance Stroll
driver:STR.summary: Lance Stroll is a Canadian Formula One driver currently racing for Aston Martin in the sport's top racing series.

driver:TSU.title: Yuki Tsunoda
driver:TSU.summary: Yuki Tsunoda is a Japanese driver currently working as a reserve for both Red Bull Racing and Racing Bulls after competing in Formula One as a full-time racer from 2021 through 2025.

driver:VER.title: Max Verstappen
driver:VER.summary: The Dutch racing driver has secured four consecutive Formula One world championships between 2021 and 2024 while representing Red Bull Racing. With 71 Grand Prix victories accumulated over 12 seasons, he stands as one of the sport's most dominant performers in the modern era.

driver:ZHO.title: Zhou Guanyu
driver:ZHO.summary: Zhou Guanyu holds the distinction of being China's sole competitor in Formula One history, having raced in the championship from 2022 to 2024. He currently functions as a reserve driver for the Cadillac team in the sport.

team:Alpine.title: Alpine F1 Team
team:Alpine.summary: The Enstone-based team has competed as Alpine since 2021, inheriting Renault's works team status following a rebranding of the long-established Renault F1 operation. Operating with a French licence and powered by Mercedes engines, Alpine achieved its only victory when Esteban Ocon won the 2021 Hungarian Grand Prix, before Renault's withdrawal from the sport concluded the team's tenure at the end of 2025.

team:Aston Martin.title: Aston Martin in Formula One
team:Aston Martin.summary: Aston Martin, a British automotive manufacturer, has competed in Formula One through different organizational structures, with the current iteration operating as AMR GP Limited under the Aston Martin Aramco Formula One Team banner.

team:Ferrari.title: Scuderia Ferrari
team:Ferrari.summary: Scuderia Ferrari HP, the racing arm of Italian luxury automaker Ferrari, stands as Formula One's longest-running and most accomplished team, competing continuously since the championship's inaugural 1950 season. The squad, colloquially termed the "Prancing Horse" after their iconic emblem, has maintained an uninterrupted presence throughout Formula One's entire history.

team:Haas F1 Team.title: Haas F1 Team
team:Haas F1 Team.summary: Gene Haas established this American-licensed Formula One team in 2014, with the squad entering the championship in 2016. Ayao Komatsu currently leads the team as principal, taking over from Guenther Steiner who held the position since the team's founding until early 2024.

team:Kick Sauber.title: Sauber Motorsport
team:Kick Sauber.summary: Sauber Motorsport AG, a Swiss racing constructor founded by Peter Sauber in 1970, established itself through endurance racing success including a 1989 Le Mans victory before entering Formula One in 1993. The team competed in the sport for over three decades, becoming the fourth-longest-running constructor by race entries before being acquired by Audi AG in 2024 to serve as the foundation for Audi's Formula One programme.

team:McLaren.title: McLaren
team:McLaren.summary: McLaren Racing is a British Formula One outfit headquartered in Woking that competes under corporate sponsorship arrangements. The squad operates as part of the broader McLaren Group structure, with ownership held by Bahraini investment firm Mumtalakat Holding Company.

team:Mercedes.title: Mercedes-AMG Petronas F1 Team
team:Mercedes.summary: Mercedes has competed in Formula One as both a constructor and engine supplier since 1954, with its current team based in Brackley and operating under a German licence. The operation, now known as Mercedes-AMG Petronas Formula One Team, became a three-way partnership in 2022 when Ineos joined Mercedes-Benz Group and Toto Wolff as equal stakeholders. The marque's racing heritage is synonymous with the "Silver Arrows" nickname.

team:Racing Bulls.title: Racing Bulls
team:Racing Bulls.summary: Visa Cash App Racing Bulls is an Italian Formula One constructor that entered the sport in 2024 as the second team under Red Bull GmbH's ownership, alongside Red Bull Racing. Based in Faenza with a secondary facility near its sister team in Milton Keynes, the squad operates as one of two Red Bull-affiliated constructors competing in the championship.

team:RB.title: Racing Bulls
team:RB.summary: Visa Cash App Racing Bulls is an Italian Formula One team and constructor that commenced operations in 2024 as the second constructor owned by Red Bull GmbH. Headquartered in Faenza with a secondary facility near Milton Keynes, the squad operates as a sister team to Red Bull Racing within the same corporate structure.

team:Red Bull Racing.title: Red Bull Racing
team:Red Bull Racing.summary: Oracle Red Bull Racing is an Austrian-licensed Formula One team based in England, owned by Red Bull GmbH since its 2005 establishment. Led by Christian Horner until 2025, the team recently transitioned leadership to Laurent Mekies as part of Red Bull's two-team F1 operation.

team:Williams.title: Williams Racing
team:Williams.summary: Williams Grand Prix Engineering stands as a British Formula One constructor founded in 1977 by Frank Williams and Patrick Head, emerging from the remnants of Williams's previous failed racing venture. Based in Grove, Oxfordshire, the team competes in the 2026 season as Atlassian Williams F1 Team and operates from a substantial 60-acre facility.
